gloss: palanquin; sedan chair; a covered litter carried on poles by bearers

definitions.gloss: palanquin; sedan chair; a covered litter carried on poles by bearers
definitions.explanation: A traditional Japanese conveyance consisting of a cabin mounted on horizontal poles, carried by two or more bearers. Used primarily during the Edo period for transporting nobility and wealthy individuals.

examples.japanese: ⟦{殿様|とのさま}→殿様：10455_tonosama⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{駕籠|かご}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{乗|の}って→乗る：00511_noru⟧⟦{城|しろ}→城：03255_shiro⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{出|で}た→出る：00513_deru⟧。
examples.english: The lord left the castle riding in a palanquin.

examples.english: In period dramas, scenes of samurai women riding in palanquins for their wedding procession are often depicted.

notes:
A traditional Japanese means of transportation in which a person sits inside a cabin mounted on poles, carried by two or more bearers ({駕籠|かご}{掻|か}き). Used primarily during the Edo period by the nobility, samurai class, and wealthy merchants. Different from ⟦{籠|かご}→籠：02577_kago⟧ (basket/cage), which shares the same reading.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {駕籠|かご}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{乗|の}る→乗る：00511_noru⟧: to ride in a palanquin
- {駕籠|かご}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{担|かつ}ぐ→担ぐ：03917_katsugu⟧: to carry a palanquin
- {駕籠|かご}{掻|か}き: palanquin bearer
- お{駕籠|かご}: palanquin (polite)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{籠|かご}→籠：02577_kago⟧: basket, cage — same reading, different meaning
- {御輿|みこし}: portable shrine — carried on poles, but for religious festivals
- ⟦{人力車|じんりきしゃ}→人力車：11472_jinrikisha⟧: rickshaw — later form of human-powered transport
